The main reason solar is expensive to install (t certified installer) is the home batteries and DC to AC conversion equipment as well as all of the wire. Everything runs on AC power, solar generates and charges DC, home battery kits are getting cheaper but still are a few thousand and have to be replaced every 5-10 years.

You will need to test the soil conditions anywhere you are going to ranch/grow, the north east has a lot of mineral deficiencies such as magnesium and a few others which cause cattle to become sick, most ranchers have to get special salt blocks to supplement the minerals, same with crops lacking certain compounds, fertilizer compounds are needed and can get expensive, yes composting yourself is a big money saver, but won't mean anything if you do not have the proper nitrates.

Weed grows almost anywhere and can become a good cash crop, weeds are well weeds.

Sanitation is a big issue, septic tanks are fine, a family of 4 can get away with a 5kgal tank if it is treated properly for 10 years without pumping. (I have been out of the septic business for awhile but for 10+ people you will need 2x5k tanks and area set aside for leech fields, if the area is remote you will need to build a dirt/stone road and in 40 acres you are looking at several thousand feet of road/compaction/stone/laydown yard. The equipment to scrape and level/dig such things can be expensive to own, cheaper to lease, but still looking at hundreds per day. Logistics are a nightmare without proper planning. (FYI septic tanks alone without pumps/pipes install are about 1k a piece.)

So digging a well and having a safe system installed would net about 5k-15k upfront investment, not counting any plumbing you would need for irrigation and potable supplies.
